Hi Olivia — thank you, and glad the demo landed well.

I've attached two artifacts: a) a 3-scenario capacity plan in the spreadsheet (conservative / base / aggressive) that maps sku mixes to expected token throughput, and b) a short MA draft for our commercial terms. Key notes up-front:

- Scenario sensitivity: our modeling shows that a 20% GPU cost increase reduces available margin by ~8–10% on the base plan; at 40% it's ~15–18% (see tab "Cost Sensitivity").
- Discount guardrails: standard approval for up to 15% list discount is delegated to commercial managers; anything between 15–25% requires CSM + Sales Director sign-off; >25% is an exec escalation (VP Sales + Finance).
- Term trade-offs: 24-month tenor smooths unit price by ~6% vs 12-month but increases exposure if market falls — we can add an annual true-up or a capped indexation clause.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached modeling with your finance/procurement.
2) If you want a firm quote for the base and aggressive scenarios, we can produce an SOW and internal approval request (I will loop in Finance).
3) If EdgeScale needs deeper protection for GPU market shocks, we can propose a priced protection (tiered credits / rebate) to limit pass-through.

I'm looping in Lauren (pricing) and Karthik (strategic deals) to confirm the approval ladder and any model we should run for the 30% discount ask.

Best,

Marcus / Karthik — reviewed Marcus' modeling overnight. Quick summary for the record:

- The "Cost Sensitivity" tab is sound; we validated assumptions on utilization and GPU-backed unit cost. If markets spike +40% the only lever that preserves gross margin is deeper discounting (customer share of market move) or adding a rebate/credit structure tied to GPU index.
- Pricing approach for EdgeScale: offer a 12-month base with an opt-in 12-month extension (two-step) or 24-month firm. For 24-month firm: we can offer ~8–10% off list at scale for the base scenario (no special approvals).
- Governance/approvals: up to 15% — Commercial Manager approval (auto). 15–25% — Requires Pricing Director sign-off + Finance. 25–35% — Needs VP Sales + Head of Finance review and Finance model. 35%+ — hammer case; require executive sign-off and likely require revenue protections (rebates or clawbacks).

If EdgeScale insists on a 30% starting discount across the board, we need: a) a clear committed spend schedule, b) multi-year payment terms or escrow, and c) an approved finance model (I'm happy to run it but will need the detailed sku mix).

Happy to jump on a 30–40 minute call with procurement tomorrow morning to walk through options.

- Lauren
Principal Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference
